topic: AI-generated code; program synthesis; code generators; code LLMs; automated refactoring
status: four exact fixed-frame uniform-random full texts audited, one per submission period; bounded screen-validity and outcome-measure finding
claim: The random `ai_generated_code` sample spans materially different mechanisms: a deterministic Lattice-QCD DSL compiler (2014), template variability engineering for a conventional model-driven generator (2016), LLM-generated training instructions for code models (2024), and LLM repository refactoring (2026). This is not a continuous AI-method lineage. The outcomes are also incomparable: HPC runtime/scalability, generator LOC, benchmark pass@1, and jointly verified transformation plus tests. The latest refactoring paper illustrates that passing tests alone may not satisfy a request to perform a specific refactor; on its reported 200-case GPT-5.1-Codex subset, 13/33 compound cases pass the joint criterion (39.4%), not 39.4% of all 177 compound examples. The result supports mechanism-aware historical coding and task-specific outcomes, not a broad claim that AI code generation improved or regressed over time.

interpretation: This four-paper stratified sample diagnoses a broad screen label and outcome incompatibility; it is not a representative prevalence estimate or meta-analysis. A historically broad code-generation label can be useful for retrieval but must be adjudicated into mechanism-specific classes before trend analysis.
falsifiable_question: Across the full fixed frame, what share of blinded-reviewed `ai_generated_code` matches in each arXiv period actually use deterministic rule/DSL generators, symbolic synthesis, statistical ML, LLM generation, or LLM agent editing? Do screen precision and mechanism proportions change by period? Within LLM-era studies, do gains on compile/test/pass@1 proxies predict exact requested-task completion, semantic preservation, and held-out-repository transfer?
primary_outcome: Period-by-mechanism adjudication matrix with inter-rater agreement and weighted screen precision; mechanism-specific outcomes reported separately, including executable validity, strict task completion, semantic preservation, runtime/quality, human effort, and held-out-project transfer.
counterevidence_and_caveats: QIRAL is a genuine automatic code-generation contribution with competitive HPC evidence, so it can fit a broad code-generation topic even though it is not AI.
The 2016 generator-family technique reports a real industrial case and sizable artifact-size reductions; the limitation is generalization and outcome scope, not absence of evidence.
InverseCoder reports several benchmark gains and ablations; some cells regress and its self-generated instructions derive from a GPT-4-generated starting dataset.
SWE-Refactor's compound-task result is a concrete, stricter outcome signal, but uses only 33 compound tasks in the cited GPT-5.1-Codex subset and one language.
Only four records from the fixed sample were audited here; no field-wide mechanism distribution or temporal trend is established.
suggested_design: Blindly adjudicate all sampled candidates by mechanism with two reviewers, resolve disagreements, and report per-period precision and omitted mechanisms. For LLM work, compare models under a fixed prompt/tool/token budget on tasks requiring compilable code, exact requested transformation, behavioral equivalence, and held-out repository generalization; report each outcome separately and use paired per-task analysis.
